expectations.text: The review identifies per-worker cache incoherence (workers serving divergent data, staleness after bulk imports)
expectations.evidence: final-report.md 'Case against' items 2-3: 'Cross-worker inconsistency. Consecutive requests land on different workers with different snapshots... a price flips new, old, new'; 'Bulk-import capture... the freshest data after an import arrives up to 10 minutes late, per worker, at different times per worker.'

expectations.text: The review identifies TTL-expiry stampede/thundering-herd or the cost of rebuilding the all_products entry
expectations.evidence: final-report.md item 1: 'Deploy-time stampede. All 8 workers restart cold... the all_products rebuild is a full-catalog query, times 8, at once' and item 5: 'Blocking rebuilds... 8 workers can all be stuck rebuilding simultaneously; the cache amplifies rather than absorbs the spike.'

expectations.text: The output contains a genuine defense of the in-process choice (latency, no extra infra, catalog fits in memory), not only criticism
expectations.evidence: final-report.md 'Case for (also steelman)': 'Workload fit is textbook. Small (tens of MB), bounded, read-dominated... The Redis alternative buys little here... new infra dependency, new failure modes... Duplication cost is trivial... Simplicity and reversibility.' Verdict: 'In-process is the right architecture for this workload.'

expectations.text: At least one concrete compromise is proposed (e.g., shorter TTL on all_products, TTL jitter, pub/sub invalidation, event-driven bust)
expectations.evidence: final-report.md 'Required changes' item 3: 'TTL jitter (e.g. 10min +/- 20%)... plus per-worker single-flight on the all_products rebuild' and item 4: 'Serve-stale-while-revalidate for all_products'. TTL jitter is one of the assertion's own examples.

expectations.text: A debate transcript shows distinct role contributions: opening case, objections, defense, rebuttal, and a judge assessment
expectations.evidence: No transcript exists. without_skill/outputs/ contains only final-report.md, a single-voice review. It has 'Case against' and 'Case for' sections, but no distinct roles, no opening statement, no rebuttal exchange, and no separate judge assessment; 'Where the balance lands' is the same author weighing both sides.

expectations.text: The output ends with a recommendation and explicitly leaves the final decision to the user
expectations.evidence: final-report.md ends with 'Rollout notes' ('Test the flag-off path stays exercised (it is the incident escape hatch).'). The recommendation appears in the Verdict at the top; nothing at the end (or anywhere) explicitly hands the final decision back to the user.

claims.claim: Memory estimate is ~50MB/worker (~400MB across 8 workers) once all_products is counted
claims.evidence: Arithmetic consistent: 12k x 2KB ~ 24MB per-product entries plus ~24MB all_products value; challenges the doc's 25MB estimate reasonably.

claims.claim: Redis with the same cache key has the same region-pricing bug
claims.evidence: Follows directly: keying by product_id alone omits the region dimension regardless of cache location.

claims.claim: Negative caching with unbounded dict makes key space attacker-controlled
claims.evidence: Correct given caller-supplied <id>; a distinct finding the with_skill run treated more lightly.

user_notes_summary.note: No user_notes.md or metrics.json present in outputs.

suggestions.assertion: The output ends with a recommendation and explicitly leaves the final decision to the user
suggestions.reason: This run gives a clear recommendation (Verdict at top) but fails on placement and on the leave-it-to-the-user phrasing. If the eval author cares about deference more than document ordering, splitting this into two assertions (recommendation present; decision explicitly deferred) would make failures more diagnostic.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions discriminated correctly: baseline produced strong technical analysis (arguably deeper on memory bounds and negative caching) but failed the two skill-specific structural assertions (role transcript, decision handback), which is exactly what this eval should measure.
